title: Microsoft Teams: mandatory pre-meeting consent for meeting participants
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record, Microsoft's tenant notice and the cited documentation. Its controls match the documented steps and commands, and it explicitly reports the conflicting preview and release-status statements.

claims.claim: Teams supports an admin-configured mandatory custom consent message before meeting joins.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can configure a custom consent message that participants must accept before they can join meetings hosted by organizers in your organization.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Pre-meeting consent is controlled through Teams meeting policies.
claims.quote: Pre-meeting consent is controlled through Teams meeting policies and is turned off by default.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in and off by default.
claims.quote: The feature is disabled by default and requires admin configuration

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].scope; Governance controls; Change & support
claims.claim: Consent applies to meetings organised by users assigned the enabled policy, so policy assignment determines its reach.
claims.quote: When enabled, the consent experience applies to meetings organized by users who are assigned the policy.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: All participants, including organisers, internal users, external users and anonymous attendees, must accept before joining.
claims.quote: All meeting participants, including organizers, internal users, external users, and anonymous attendees, must accept the consent message before joining.

claims.where: What's changing; Security & identity; Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A participant who does not accept the message cannot join the meeting.
claims.quote: If a participant doesn't accept the consent message, they can't join the meeting.

claims.claim: Consent content can include terms and conditions, disclaimers, recording notices and responsible AI usage guidelines.
claims.quote: You can present custom terms and conditions, disclaimers, recording notices, responsible AI usage guidelines, and other compliance-related statements to meeting participants.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Admins can configure one default language and up to four additional languages, five total.
claims.quote: You can specify one default language and up to four additional languages.

claims.claim: Participants see consent content based on their device language settings.
claims.quote: Participants see the consent message based on their device language settings.

claims.claim: The default language is used when the participant's device language is not configured.
claims.quote: If a participant's device language isn’t configured in the policy, the content from the default language is shown to the participant.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The consent message can contain up to 1,500 characters.
claims.quote: Compose your message. The message can contain up to 1,500 characters.

claims.claim: Admins can preview the participant experience before saving.
claims.quote: After you add your custom consent message, you can preview the participant experience before saving the policy.

claims.claim: Participant consent acknowledgements are stored in audit logs for compliance, reporting and investigations.
claims.quote: Consent acknowledgments are recorded in audit logs to support governance, investigations, and transparency.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature's Learn page marks it as currently in Public Preview.
claims.quote: This feature is currently in Public Preview.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference says EnablePreMeetingConsent has no effect because the feature is not fully released.
claims.quote:
### -EnablePreMeetingConsent
This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference gives the same not-fully-released and no-effect warning for PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier.
claims.quote:
### -PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier
This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: The enablement path is Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Enable pre-meeting participant consent.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
Under Meeting join & lobby, turn the Enable pre-meeting participant consent toggle On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EnablePreMeetingConsent $true is the documented enablement command, subject to the reference warning reported in the briefing.
claims.quote:
-Identity: Specify the name of the policy being created.
-EnablePreMeetingConsent: $true: All participants must explicitly accept a custom consent dialog before joining any meeting hosted by the tenant.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Customize message is reached after enabling the consent toggle in the chosen policy's Meeting join & lobby section.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
Under Meeting join & lobby, turn the Enable pre-meeting participant consent toggle On.
Select Customize message.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: New-CsPreMeetingConsent -LocalizedContent <localized content> creates consent content.
claims.quote:
Create localized consent content. You can configure up to five languages, with one language set as the default:
$consent = New-CsPreMeetingConsent `
    -LocalizedContent @(
        $englishContent
        $frenchContent
    )

claims.claim: EnablePreMeetingConsent defaults to False.
claims.quote:
### -EnablePreMeetingConsent
| Type: | Boolean |
| Default value: | False |

claims.claim: The enabled policy must have consent content configured.
claims.quote: Requires at least one consent content entry configured in TeamsPreMeetingConsentConfiguration.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy assigns the returned content identifier with -PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier.
claims.quote:
Copy the configuration identifier returned by New-CsPreMeetingConsent:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy `
    -Identity $policyIdentity `
    -PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier $consentId `
    -EnablePreMeetingConsent $true

claims.claim: The guide instructs administrators to remove assignments from all meeting policies before deleting a consent configuration.
claims.quote: Before deleting a configuration, remove the content assignment from all meeting policies.

claims.claim: Consent content is a separate configuration object referenced by meeting policies, rather than an individual participant setting.
claims.quote:
List all pre-meeting consent configurations:
Get-CsPreMeetingConsent
Assign the consent content to a meeting policy and enable pre-meeting consent:

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Pre-meeting consent does not currently apply to the originator initiating an ad-hoc channel meeting.
claims.quote:
Pre-meeting consent doesn't currently apply to the following meeting scenarios:
- Originator initiating an ad-hoc meeting in a channel.

claims.claim: Pre-meeting consent does not currently apply when accepting an incoming direct meeting-join request on mobile.
claims.quote:
Pre-meeting consent doesn't currently apply to the following meeting scenarios:
- Accepting an incoming direct request to join a meeting on mobile.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance

claims.claim: The feature can be configured through the Teams admin center or PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can enable and configure pre-meeting consent in the Teams admin center or by using PowerShell.

claims.claim: Administrators can use an existing policy or create a new custom policy instead of using Global.
claims.quote: Either select an existing policy or create a new one. To apply changes to all users in your organization who don't have an existing policy assignment, use the Global policy. To exclude certain users from the global policy, create and assign a custom meeting policy.

claims.claim: Participant agreement for recording and transcription is a different meeting policy option from pre-meeting consent.
claims.quote:
Within your chosen policy, navigate to the Recording & Transcription section.
Toggle the Require participant agreement for recording and transcription setting On or Off.

claims.claim: The feature guide describes no agent or automated action beyond the participant consent experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams pre-meeting consent agent automated actions. Read the full pre-meeting-consent guide and returned excerpts; the guide describes participant consent and administrative configuration, not an agent performing actions.

claims.claim: The pre-meeting consent guide does not explain how Teams Rooms, PSTN dial-in participants or meeting bots meet this requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams pre-meeting consent administrator role Teams Rooms PSTN bots audit activity. Read pre-meeting-consent and returned excerpts; the feature guide gives no such endpoint handling. Recording-consent endpoint rules concern a different setting.
